title: Contextual Tripwire Matrix for Automated Evictions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a contextual tripwire matrix that fuses latency, error-rate, token-cost, and throughput signals into an actionable composite score per deployment cohort (canary/A-B/shadow). The system will support per-customer baselines, cohort-aware hysteresis, and cost-normalized thresholds so automated evictions (rollbacks/fallbacks/traffic drains) are defensible and explainable. This ticket covers design, implementation, and initial rollout for runtime-1.36.
background: Current canary safeguards use mostly single-signal thresholds (eg. p95 latency or 5xx rate). That produces noisy aborts during traffic spikes or for high-cost token workloads. We observed two false-positive rollbacks in Q4 2025 driven by transient concurrency spikes, and one missed rollback where token-cost drifted without latency change. We need a composite approach that understands context: traffic pattern, customer cohort, model size, and token mix.
proposal: Build a tripwire matrix service that: 1) computes normalized signal values for latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate (5xx, hallucination proxies), token-cost (cost-per-response normalized to baseline tokens), and throughput (rps); 2) combines into a weighted composite score per cohort using configurable weights and friction windows; 3) applies cohort-specific hysteresis and dynamic thresholds (percentile baselines or MAD-based bands); 4) emits an actionable verdict (NOOP, ALERT, SLOW-FALLBACK, DRAIN-TRAFFIC, ROLLBACK) and a rationale blob for audit/console. Integrate with rollout controller to execute actions and with Console to show signal breakdown and replayable synthetic probes.
design_notes: Composite score = sum(w_i * norm(signal_i)) where norm maps raw signal to a 0-1 risk band using historical cohort percentiles (e.g., 75th-95th -> 0.3-0.8) and outlier clamping.
Use multiple aggregation windows: short-term (30s), mid-term (5m), and long-term (1h). Short-term triggers increase sensitivity but respect hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.
Token-cost normalization divides observed cost by cohort baseline cost-per-response; for A/B with differing models, normalize by model-class baseline.

Hysteresis: require composite score > threshold for T_short OR score > higher_threshold for T_mid to actuate permanent actions; support graceful actions first (SLOW-FALLBACK) before aggressive (ROLLBACK).
Cohort baselining: for new customers/cohorts with insufficient history use model-family priors and higher default thresholds to avoid noisy behavior.
Explainability: verdict must include top-3 contributing signals with relative weights and recent trend lines for traceability in Console and incident postmortems.
Privacy/security: tripwire metadata must not include raw prompt text; only hashed identifiers and aggregated metrics are emitted to the control plane.
Fail-safe: on control-plane connectivity loss, rollout controller should degrade to read-only and not evict; local runtime prober will keep history and perform local slowdown if needed.
Operational knobs in Console: per-customer disable, manual hold, emergency rollback, and dry-run for policies.

We will implement signal fusion service as a sidecar-compatible microservice that subscribes to metrics stream (Kafka) and writes verdicts to a rollout queue (Kafka topic) consumed by rollout-controller.
Performance goal: verdict latency < 2s for short-window decisions; storage retention for raw aggregates 30d; explainability payload < 2KB per verdict.

Trade-offs: heavier stateful baselining increases accuracy but raises memory/storage on workers. We opt for compressed EWMAs + reservoir sampling for percentile approximations to balance accuracy and footprint.
acceptance_criteria: Tripwire service computes composite score for each active cohort and emits verdicts to rollout queue.
Console shows per-verdict rationale with top-3 signals and trend sparklines.
End-to-end automated action chain: verdict -> rollout-controller -> SLOW-FALLBACK -> DRAIN-TRAFFIC -> ROLLBACK works in staging with synthetic traffic harness.
False positive rate for canary aborts reduced by >= 40% compared to baseline single-signal policy on the Q4-2025 replay dataset.
Throughput: system sustains 2k verdicts/sec across clusters with 99th percentile latency < 2s in our staging deployment.
Security: no raw prompts are included in emitted rationale; SAST review passed for tripwire service code.
Runbook and Grafana dashboard added; runbook includes escalation path and manual override steps.
metrics_and_signals: Latency: p50/p95/p99 response time (ms) per cohort and per model-family
Error rate: 5xx, invalid-responses, hallucination proxy (semantic mismatch scoring) per cohort
Token-cost: token-cost-per-response normalized to cohort baseline
Throughput: requests/sec and concurrency per cohort
Resource signals: GPU queue depth, memory pressure (to detect infra-caused latencies)
Synthetic probe health: periodic synthetic requests with known outputs for quality checks
threshold_strategy: Multi-tier thresholds: soft (alert), medium (automatic graceful mitigation), hard (automatic rollback). Soft thresholds map to cohort percentile crossings (e.g., >90th for 5m window). Medium thresholds require composite score > 0.6 for 2 consecutive mid-term windows. Hard thresholds require composite score > 0.85 OR simultaneous extreme on two orthogonal signals (eg. p99 latency spike + token-cost drift). Use MAD-based bands for non-Gaussian signals and percentile fallback for low-history cohorts.
testing_plan: Offline replay: run the matrix against Q4-2025 production traces plus synthetic spike scenarios to evaluate ROC for abort decisions.
Staging A/B: enable tripwire in dry-run mode for 2 weeks comparing to legacy policy; collect recommendations but do not actuate.
Canary actuations: roll out active policy to 5% progressive traffic with explicit canary cohort; require manual approval at 5% and 20% gates before full activation.
Chaos tests: inject infra pressure (GPU throttling, delayed KV) to ensure tripwire distinguishes infra vs model regressions.
Customer safety net: a per-customer auto-exempt if customer-set label disables auto-eviction; metric to measure exemption usage.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design & infra): build tripwire service, integrate with metrics stream and rollout queue - 2 sprints.
Phase 1 (Dry-run staging): replay historical traces, expose recommendations in Console (no actuation) - 1 sprint.
Phase 2 (Limited actuations): enable SLOW-FALLBACK for internal tenants and non-critical customer cohorts at 5% traffic - 1 sprint + monitoring window.
Phase 3 (Widened actuations): enable DRAIN-TRAFFIC & ROLLBACK for low-risk workloads with 20% progressive ramp and manual approvals - 2 sprints.
Phase 4 (GA): full policy, training docs, runbook, and retrospective - release runtime-1.36.
Rollback safety: Manual kill-switch in Console and an automated cooldown that prevents more than one full rollback per deployment per 24h unless escalated.
open_questions: How should we weight token-cost vs latency for different customer SLAs? Suggest user-configurable profiles (latency-first, cost-first, balanced).
What is acceptable default for new customers with no historical baseline? Proposal: 95th-percentile priors from model-family plus +20% buffer.
Should we expose composite score API for customers to consume? Security/UX trade-offs to evaluate.
Exact trend-window durations and hysteresis multipliers: currently proposed 30s/5m/1h but subject to tuning after dry-run.
Integration with Dedicated environments: will tripwire run in the control plane or provide a local mode to respect air-gapped constraints?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy signals cause flip-flop rollbacks. Mitigation: multi-window hysteresis, require corroboration across signals, dry-run period.
Risk: privacy leak in rationale blobs. Mitigation: strict schema with no text fields, SAST review, and field-level redaction.
Risk: resource overhead on runtime nodes. Mitigation: move heavy baselining to central service; use summarized aggregates on nodes.
Risk: customers dependent on small latency improvements may see unintended behavior. Mitigation: expose customer profile and opt-out; provide simulated impact before activation.
